text: {"score":2,"justification":"Numbers match the card, but the interpretation is poorly grounded and internally contradictory. The summary concludes the pattern is consistent with a high-acuity panel and recommends not pursuing recovery, while its own evidence shows 18.4% 99215 vs 4.5% expected (4.1x, risk-adjusted score 10.5, z 2.61). 99215 share is above the all-provider share at every complexity tier (e.g., 14.6% vs 5.2% at 2 conditions, 22% vs 8% at 3, 40% vs 12% at 4, 53% vs 22% at 5+), so the excess is not explained by a complex panel. The headline is also misleading: 3.9% vs 2.8% is a single low-complexity tier, while the stronger gaps elsewhere are ignored. The next step claims 'documentation returned supports the level billed', but zero records were returned, which contradicts the summary's own statement. The cited examples are only high-complexity claims, which don't show anything about the concern; none of the 25 low-complexity 99215 claims are cited, and no request for documentation is suggested.","problems":["Conclusion 'consistent with legitimate acuity' contradicts risk-adjusted evidence (4.1x expected, score 10.5, elevated in every complexity tier).","Next step says 'documentation returned supports the level billed' although 0 records were returned; factually false and self-contradictory.","Recommending against recovery with no documentation reviewed is unsupported and not cautious.","Headline cherry-picks the 0-condition tier (3.9% vs 2.8%) and ignores much larger gaps in other tiers.","Cited example claims are only high-complexity 99215s; low-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0098352, C0097638) that matter to an investigator are not cited.","No next step to request records for 99215 visits, despite documentation being absent; the missing documentation is mentioned but not acted on."]}
